notes: How this part was researched: the session's shared web-search allowance ran out after about twenty searches. Everything else was read directly with the kit's honest User-Agent, each site's robots.txt obeyed (through ballot.local_sites' polite fetcher), or with the reading tool: the candidates' own sites, county and school district sites, the Democratic Party of Wisconsin's and county parties' pages, the American Solidarity Party's page, Wikipedia, and WisPolitics. A voter guide (The Ballot Brief) and Wikipedia's links were used only to learn campaign addresses; each address was then opened and is recorded only where the site itself names the candidate and the office.

Party pages: the entries under endorsed_by are lists of a party's own candidates ("Our Candidates", "Your 2026 Republican Ticket", a candidate page marked "Current Candidate"), not statements using the word "endorse"; the unit text says so for the second reader to judge. The La Crosse County Republican Party's site says "Candidate pages are not an endorsement", so nothing is recorded from it for Jim Green. No Republican party page was found naming Rice, Maze, Kjorlie or Severson.

Not recorded: adamneylon.com (the address Wikipedia gives for Adam Neylon) is today titled "Adam Neylon for Waukesha County Executive", a different race, so he has no website here. steffen4wisconsin.com (David Steffen) and robkreibich.com ask scripts to stay out in robots.txt and were not read. The City of Marshfield's site asks scripts to stay out, so nothing was read about Krista J. James. Sauk County's coroner page names the present coroner only; nothing was found about Amber Giddings. Nothing was found for Jim Green or Jeffrey L. Mursau (no campaign site found), nor a site of his or her own for Nathan Tataje, Aleaner Pabonnie, Mark Becker or Travis Maze.
Sitting legislators (Madison, Neylon, Kreibich, August, Mursau, Steffen, Roe, Tucker, Subeck, Maxey, Moses, Marklein) were looked up only for a website and endorsements, as the rules say.
A voter guide says Mark Becker was a Brown County supervisor and chaired the Republican Party of Brown County; no official or named news page stating it was opened, so it is not recorded.
